title: Superpositions on a characteristic cone
notes: The notes call \(\int_{P(\xi)=0}f((x,\xi))A(\xi)\,d\xi\) the general solution of the homogeneous equation, with arbitrary \(f,A\), and attribute a singularity description to Borovikov.
statement: If \(P\) is a homogeneous polynomial of degree \(m\), each smooth ridge function \(x\mapsto f(x\cdot\xi)\) with \(P(\xi)=0\) satisfies \(P(\partial_x)f(x\cdot\xi)=0\). Any superposition for which differentiation under the integral is valid is likewise a solution. Exhaustion of all local or global solutions requires a specified real or complex characteristic cycle, solution space and amplitude class.
reconstruction: The checked elementary ridge-function assertion is separated from the unverified completeness claim. For an elliptic real symbol, its real characteristic cone may reduce to the origin, so an ordinary integral over that cone cannot represent all harmonic functions.
fate: Borovikov\textquotesingle s 1959 paper is the named antecedent \citep{borovikov1959fundamental}. The fragment does not identify a precise completeness or singular-support theorem from that paper. The unrestricted phrase \textquotedblleft general solution\textquotedblright{} is therefore not certified.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: the construction has a classical antecedent; the exact completeness and singularity claim intended in the notebook remains unidentified.

title: Homogeneous powers and normalized distributions
notes: The displayed example has \((x,\xi)^\lambda/\Gamma(\lambda+1)\) under the characteristic-surface integral and refers to \(R_0^+\).
statement: The one-variable distributions \(t_+^\lambda/\Gamma(\lambda+1)\), initially defined for \(\operatorname{Re}\lambda>-1\), have an entire distribution-valued continuation and satisfy \(\partial_t(t_+^\lambda/\Gamma(\lambda+1))=t_+^{\lambda-1}/\Gamma(\lambda)\). Applying such distributions to a linear functional is a standard ingredient of homogeneous fundamental solutions. The notebook does not specify the power branch, sign, cycle or meaning of \(R_0^+\).
reconstruction: The positive-part convention is a modern example, not a recovered subscript or branch from the scan.
fate: The method belongs to the classical construction discussed by \citet{borovikov1959fundamental}; an exact formula for the unnamed operator cannot be matched from this fragment.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: identifiable method, unidentified specific fundamental solution.

title: Boundary values of reciprocal symbols
notes: A Grushin formula is written as a sum of Fourier integrals with denominator \(P(\xi)\pm i0\) and a partition of unity on the sphere.
statement: When the distributional limits \((P\pm i\varepsilon)^{-1}\to T_\pm\) exist, \(P T_\pm=1\); with the Fourier normalization fixed, \(\mathcal F^{-1}T_\pm\) is a fundamental solution of \(P(D)\). A localization partition must sum to one in the required symbol region, with the origin and any singular characteristic points treated separately.
fate: Borovikov\textquotesingle s paper is a verified nearby antecedent, but targeted searches of Grushin\textquotesingle s fundamental-solution work did not identify this exact partition formula. No unrestricted existence theorem for the \(i0\) limit is inferred.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: the formal multiplier mechanism is clear; its intended hypotheses and precise Grushin source are not.

title: Dimension threshold for entire minimal graphs
notes: The notes announce that an entire minimal graph \(z=f(x_1,\ldots,x_{n-1})\) is a plane for \(n\leq8\), and that the assertion fails for \(n\geq9\), naming De Giorgi, Simons and Bombieri.
statement: For a smooth entire solution \(u:\mathbb R^m\to\mathbb R\) of the minimal-surface equation, every graph is affine when \(m\leq7\). Non-affine entire minimal graphs exist for every \(m\geq8\). Thus the ambient dimension threshold is \(m+1=9\).
reconstruction: The variable dimension and the ambient dimension are explicitly distinguished; their one-unit difference explains the threshold in the notebook.
fate: The counterexamples of \citet{bombieridegiorgigiusti1969minimal} settle the remaining high-dimensional direction. This is an announcement of an already obtained result, continuing the earlier seminar occurrence 1966-114.6, rather than a new unsolved question.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope; no open problem is asserted by this item.

title: Pointwise spectral measure and projector kernel
notes: For a self-adjoint operator \(A\), a spectral interval \(\Lambda\), and a point \(x_0\), the notes set \(M_{x_0}(\Lambda)=\max|f(x_0)|^2\) over unit vectors in the spectral subspace and introduce its projector kernel.
statement: Let \(A\) be self-adjoint on \(L^2(X,\mu)\) with spectral projections \(E(\Lambda)\). If evaluation at \(x\) is a well-defined bounded functional on \(E(\Lambda)L^2\), then its squared norm is \(\sup_{\|u\|=1,u\in E(\Lambda)L^2}|u(x)|^2\). When \(E(\Lambda)\) has a sufficiently regular reproducing kernel this equals \(K_\Lambda(x,x)\). Compatible point evaluations give the usual positive local spectral measure.
fate: This is the classical spectral-function construction; see \citet[definition of the spectral function]{hormander1968spectral}. Density of continuous vectors alone does not ensure bounded evaluation, existence of a maximum, or a regular projector kernel.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope; no open problem is asserted by this item.
speaker: D. A. Kazhdan and I. N. Bernstein

title: Spectral convergence under domain exhaustion
notes: The heading says convergence of the spectrum as the domains increase, accompanied by nested-domain sketches and the preceding local measure.
statement: To formulate a convergence theorem one must specify domains \(X_j\uparrow X\), the realizations and boundary conditions of the operators, a common Hilbert-space comparison, and whether the conclusion concerns resolvents, spectral projections or local spectral measures. None of these data is recorded sufficiently to select one theorem.
fate: Targeted searches for Kazhdan--Bernstein spectral-measure or domain-exhaustion results, including Russian author and topic variants, did not identify a precise publication. H\"ormander\textquotesingle s spectral-function work is thematic background, not proof of the unnamed exhaustion result.

title: Analytic approximation of formal solutions
notes: The Kazhdan paragraph says that an analytic system has a formal parametric solution if and only if it has a convergent one, and that convergent solutions may be chosen arbitrarily close to the formal solution.
statement: For \(F\in\mathbb C\{x_1,\ldots,x_n,y_1,\ldots,y_m\}^r\) and \(\widehat y\in\mathbb C[[x]]^m\) with \(\widehat y(0)=0\) and \(F(x,\widehat y)=0\), every integer \(c\geq1\) admits \(y\in\mathbb C\{x\}^m\) satisfying \(F(x,y)=0\) and \(y-\widehat y\in(x)^c\mathbb C[[x]]^m\).
reconstruction: \textquotedblleft Arbitrarily close\textquotedblright{} means agreement to any prescribed finite jet in the maximal-ideal topology, not convergence of the original formal series.
fate: Published by \citet{artin1968analytic} in December 1968. The Bourbaki exposition is \citet[Thm.~1]{raynaud1969artin}, delivered by Michel Raynaud in June 1969 and printed in 1971. The notebook\textquotesingle s \textquotedblleft Artin in Bourbaki\textquotedblright{} identifies the subject, not the lecturer.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope; no open problem is asserted by this item.

title: Unilateral frictionless elastic contact
notes: On \(\Sigma\), either \(u\cdot\nu=0\) with nonnegative normal reaction and zero tangential traction, or \(u\cdot\nu>0\) with zero traction. Loads are given on \(\Sigma^*=\partial A\setminus\Sigma\).
statement: Let a bounded elastic body \(A\subset\mathbb R^d\) have a sufficiently regular boundary decomposed into a contact portion \(\Sigma\) and a loaded portion \(\Sigma^*\). With an explicitly chosen normal and stress convention, write the normal gap as \(g\geq0\) and compressive contact reaction as \(\lambda\geq0\). Frictionless contact is \(g\lambda=0\) and zero tangential reaction; prescribed traction acts on \(\Sigma^*\).
reconstruction: The modern gap/reaction variables avoid silently switching the notebook\textquotesingle s inward normal and stress convention.
fate: This is the Signorini problem treated in Fichera\textquotesingle s 1964 work and summarized before this lecture in \citet[pp.~64--66]{fichera1967unilateral}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope; no open problem is asserted by this item.

title: Strain, constitutive law and equilibrium
notes: The notebook gives \(\varepsilon_{ik}=\tfrac12(\partial_k u_i+\partial_i u_k)\), \(\sigma_{ik}+\partial W/\partial\varepsilon_{ik}=0\), and the equilibrium and traction equations.
statement: For small-strain linear elasticity, the strain is the symmetric gradient \(\varepsilon(u)\). A positive-definite quadratic energy \(W(x,\varepsilon)\) defines the conventional stress \(\tau=\partial_\varepsilon W\); with outward normal \(n\), equilibrium is \(-\operatorname{div}\tau=f\) and natural boundary traction is \(\tau n=t\). Taking \(\sigma=-\tau\) and \(\nu=-n\) recovers the sign pattern in the notebook.
fate: The constitutive and boundary conventions are explicit in \citet[pp.~64--65]{fichera1967unilateral}. They are pre-existing elastic theory, not a new sign-changing material law.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope; no open problem is asserted by this item.

title: Energy minimization and complementarity
notes: The proposed energy is the elastic energy minus work of body and surface forces; a classical minimizer in the admissible class is said to solve the contact problem, and conversely.
statement: Let \(V\) be a Sobolev displacement space, \(K\subset V\) its nonempty closed convex set satisfying the trace inequality, and \(J(u)=\tfrac12a(u,u)-\ell(u)\), with \(a\) continuous symmetric positive semidefinite. Then \(u\in K\) minimizes \(J\) exactly when \(a(u,v-u)\geq\ell(v-u)\) for all \(v\in K\). For sufficiently smooth \(u\), integration by parts gives the equilibrium, prescribed-traction and complementarity conditions.
reconstruction: The displacement must be defined throughout \(\overline A\), not merely in \(C^1(\Sigma)\), and the prescribed surface work is integrated over \(\Sigma^*\).
fate: The variational contact formulation predates the lecture; \citet[pp.~65--67]{fichera1967unilateral} gives Fichera\textquotesingle s construction. Classical differentiability is needed only to recover pointwise boundary equations.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope; no open problem is asserted by this item.

title: Weak existence and rigid-motion compatibility
notes: The classical admissible class may contain no minimizer; the discussion passes to weak minimization.
statement: If \(a\) is coercive on \(V\), \(J\) has a unique minimizer in every nonempty closed convex \(K\). In pure-traction elasticity \(a\) vanishes on rigid displacements, so one needs a quotient or normalization and compatibility of the work functional with admissible rigid directions; strict negativity in unbounded admissible directions is a typical coercivity condition. Positivity of the strain energy alone is insufficient.
reconstruction: The coercive version is stated precisely as a modern sufficient theorem; the notebook omits enough geometric and load data to state Fichera\textquotesingle s most general compatibility theorem verbatim.
fate: \citet[pp.~66--67]{fichera1967unilateral} explicitly treats the necessary work conditions and uniqueness modulo admissible rigid motions. This is an expository report of Fichera\textquotesingle s earlier solution.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope; no open problem is asserted by this item.

title: Scalar boundary-obstacle problem
notes: A scalar quadratic functional with uniformly positive coefficient matrix is introduced; on \(\Sigma\), \(u\geq0\) and either the value or the conormal derivative vanishes.
statement: Let \(a(x)\) be a bounded measurable symmetric uniformly elliptic matrix on a bounded Lipschitz domain \(A\), let \(K=\{v\in H^1(A):\operatorname{Tr}v\geq0\text{ on }\Sigma\}\), and let \(\ell(v)=\int_A fv+\int_{\Sigma^*}\varphi v\) be continuous. Minimize \(\tfrac12\int_A\nabla v\cdot a\nabla v-\ell(v)\) on \(K\), subject to coercivity or constant-direction compatibility. In a smooth realization the outward conormal derivative on \(\Sigma\) is nonnegative and complementary to \(u\).
fate: The scalar analogue is already given in \citet[pp.~66--68]{fichera1967unilateral}; later thin-obstacle regularity cannot be used to assert unrestricted classical solvability for the mixed boundary setup here.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope; no open problem is asserted by this item.

title: Necessary sign of total load
notes: The notes write \(\int_A f+\int_{\Sigma^*}\varphi\leq0\) as a necessary condition.
statement: In the scalar energy convention of the preceding item, every positive constant is an admissible recession direction. If \(J\) is bounded below on \(K\), then necessarily \(\ell(1)=\int_A f+\int_{\Sigma^*}\varphi\leq0\); otherwise \(J(u+c)\to-\infty\) as \(c\to+\infty\). This condition alone does not supply all existence or uniqueness hypotheses.
fate: The load condition is part of the classical scalar model in \citet[pp.~66--67]{fichera1967unilateral}. Its elementary recession-direction interpretation also resolves the normal-sign convention.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope; no open problem is asserted by this item.

title: Failure of classical regularity at a contact interface
notes: For signed data \(f\leq0\), \(\varphi<0\), the notebook invokes the maximum principle and Green\textquotesingle s formula and says that no \(C^1(\overline A)\) solution exists; a jump of the normal derivative is indicated.
statement: The source does not specify a complete domain, decomposition of its boundary, behavior at \(\overline\Sigma\cap\overline{\Sigma^*}\), or an explicit load. Thus the asserted universal nonexistence cannot be reconstructed as a precise theorem. Mixed contact and load interfaces can obstruct classical regularity even when the variational solution exists.
fate: Fichera\textquotesingle s pre-lecture note discusses the distinction between weak existence and regularity \citep[pp.~67--68]{fichera1967unilateral}. It is a partial contextual match; it does not justify quantifying the notebook\textquotesingle s incomplete example over all domains and loads.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: weak existence and regularity theory are established, but this particular nonexistence example is not determined by the recorded data.

title: Formal points and finite-jet approximation
notes: The rings of convergent and formal series are denoted \(A\subset B\), and formal solutions of analytic equations are approximated by convergent solutions.
statement: For the analytic system and formal solution in 1969-175.3, every prescribed finite jet is realized by an exact convergent solution. Equivalently, the analytic solution set is dense in the formal solution set for the maximal-ideal topology; this does not say that every formal solution converges.
fate: The theorem is \citet[Thm.~1]{raynaud1969artin}, reporting \citet{artin1968analytic}; both the 1968 original and June 1969 Bourbaki lecture precede this seminar.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope; no open problem is asserted by this item.

title: Parametrizing the cusp
statement: The analytic map \(y\mapsto(y^3,y^2)\) satisfies the cusp equation identically and gives its normalization near the origin. The coordinate-ring map \(\mathbb C\{x_1,x_2\}/(x_1^2-x_2^3)\to\mathbb C\{y\}\) sends \(x_1\) to \(y^3\) and \(x_2\) to \(y^2\).
reconstruction: The normalization interpretation is explanatory; the notebook records only the parametrization.
fate: This is a classical analytic-curve example illustrating the algebra used in the approximation proof, not a new parametrization claim; compare the local-ring setting of \citet[Section II]{raynaud1969artin}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope; no open problem is asserted by this item.

title: Reduction to irreducible components
notes: The argument proposes induction in dimension and writing the defining ideal as an intersection of prime ideals.
statement: Let \(R\) be a Noetherian analytic local ring and \(\phi:R\to\mathbb C[[y_1,\ldots,y_s]]\) a local homomorphism. Its kernel is prime and contains a minimal prime of \(R\), so the formal point factors through an irreducible component. Passing first to \(R_{\mathrm{red}}\) removes nilpotents; a radical ideal has a finite intersection decomposition into minimal prime ideals.
reconstruction: The domain property of the target and the passage to the reduced analytic germ are supplied explicitly.
fate: This is a standard reduction in the proof summarized by \citet[Section II]{raynaud1969artin}. An arbitrary ideal is not itself the intersection of its minimal primes unless it is radical.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope; no open problem is asserted by this item.

title: Earlier Soviet work on formal implicit functions
notes: The notes cite \ru{Покорный и Рыбкин}, Uspekhi 15(4), 1960, p.~169, and a work of Melamed in the Siberian Mathematical Journal, suggesting an earlier result.
statement: The first citation is V.~V. Pokornyi and P.~P. Rybin, on stabilization of a scalar formal implicit-function procedure. The second is identifiable as V.~B. Melamed\textquotesingle s 1965 paper. For its analytic equation in a complex Banach space, with compact linear part and one complex parameter, Theorem 1 says that all formal Puiseux solution branches converge near zero exactly when their set is finite; Theorem 2 gives a finite nonempty set of convergent branches if the zero solution at parameter zero is isolated.
reconstruction: The precise earlier statements are supplied from the papers. Their identification does not recover an unstated equivalence of hypotheses or conclusions with Artin approximation.
fate: \citet[pp.~169--172]{pokornyirybin1960formal} was received in December 1958; \citet[Theorems 1--2, p.~175]{melamed1965formal} was received 13 January 1964 and published in 1965. Both are verified earlier contributions. Their stated scalar or one-parameter convergence conclusions do not identify the notebook\textquotesingle s suggested priority comparison with the arbitrary finite-jet approximation theorem of \citet{artin1968analytic}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: both earlier references are identified and their relevant statements checked; the broad priority comparison remains too imprecise to certify.

title: Symplectic phase space and Liouville measure
notes: The notes take a \(2n\)-dimensional phase space with nondegenerate \(\Omega=d\omega\) and invariant measure \(\Omega^n\).
statement: A symplectic manifold is a smooth real \(2n\)-manifold with a closed nondegenerate real two-form \(\Omega\); its Liouville volume is \(\Omega^n/n!\). Exactness \(\Omega=d\omega\) is an additional hypothesis or a local choice. In particular a compact symplectic sphere has no globally defined primitive.
reconstruction: The exact/local distinction is necessary because the lecture subsequently takes a sphere as its example.
fate: This is classical symplectic structure underlying the orbit method \citep{kirillov1962unitary}; the line-bundle treatment in \citet[Sections 2 and 4]{kostant1970quantization} makes the global replacement for a primitive explicit.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope; no open problem is asserted by this item.

title: Hamiltonian vector fields and the Poisson bracket
notes: The correspondence \(f\mapsto X_f\) preserves brackets, and these vector fields are described as antisymmetric operators in \(L^2(M)\).
statement: Fix \(\iota_{X_f}\Omega=-df\) and \(\{f,g\}=X_f g\). Then \([X_f,X_g]=X_{\{f,g\}}\), and each Hamiltonian flow preserves Liouville volume. Consequently \(X_f\) is formally skew-symmetric on compactly supported smooth functions. A globally defined unitary flow additionally requires a complete Hamiltonian vector field; operator self-adjointness requires a domain statement.
fate: \citet[Proposition 4.1.1 and Section 4.3]{kostant1970quantization} records the Poisson-algebra homomorphism and explains why global integration is a separate requirement. The construction itself precedes the talk.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope; no open problem is asserted by this item.

title: Van Hove prequantization operator
notes: The notebook writes \(Z_f=X_f+\alpha(\omega(X_f)-f)\), attributes the construction to Van Hove (1951), and says that the bracket relation remains valid.
statement: On an exact symplectic chart with the preceding convention, \(\rho_\alpha(f)=X_f+\alpha(\omega(X_f)-f)\), acting on smooth complex functions, satisfies \([\rho_\alpha(f),\rho_\alpha(g)]=\rho_\alpha(\{f,g\})\). For real \(f\), formal skew-symmetry requires \(\alpha\in i\mathbb R\). Globally, the corresponding operators act on sections of a Hermitian line bundle with compatible connection, when its curvature class is integral.
reconstruction: Signs are fixed by the displayed Hamiltonian convention; scalar multiplication and differentiation are understood on a common smooth domain.
fate: Van Hove\textquotesingle s 1951 paper is verified bibliographically \citep{vanhove1951relations}. The full geometric operator statement is read in \citet[Theorem 4.3.1]{kostant1970quantization}. This is a prequantization construction, not an unrestricted quantization of all observables in an irreducible Hilbert-space model.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope; no open problem is asserted by this item.

title: Dependence on the prequantization parameter
notes: The operators for different values of \(\alpha\) are said to give inequivalent representations, and the language also refers to the Lie algebra of vector fields.
statement: As representations of the Poisson algebra containing constants, \(\rho_\alpha(1)=-\alpha I\), so distinct values of \(\alpha\) cannot be intertwined by a nonzero linear isomorphism. For \(\alpha\ne0\), this representation does not factor through Hamiltonian vector fields: a constant Hamiltonian has zero vector field but acts nontrivially.
fate: The precise distinction is the central extension of Hamiltonian vector fields by constants, described in \citet[Section 4.1]{kostant1970quantization}. The elementary central-character argument explains the notebook\textquotesingle s inequivalence statement.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope; no open problem is asserted by this item.

title: Polarization and the free-particle example
notes: The notes say that quantum states should depend on half the phase variables, and contrast the classical kinetic energy \(p^2/(2m)\) with the second derivative in the position variable.
statement: For \(T^*\mathbb R\), the Schr\"odinger realization uses \(L^2(\mathbb R,dq)\), \(\widehat p=-i\hbar\,d/dq\), and \(\widehat H=-(\hbar^2/2m)d^2/dq^2\), with its usual self-adjoint domain \(H^2(\mathbb R)\). A polarization is the geometric choice selecting an appropriate subspace of sections; an arbitrary choice of half the coordinates is not a coordinate-invariant definition.
reconstruction: The mass is assumed positive and the real line is boundaryless; other configuration spaces require different self-adjoint boundary conditions.
fate: \citet[Remarks 4.3.1--4.3.2]{kostant1970quantization} separates prequantization and polarized quantization. The free-particle model is standard prior quantum mechanics, not a new theorem of this seminar.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope; no open problem is asserted by this item.

title: Stereographic sphere and holomorphic generators
notes: The rotation orbit is the sphere \(x_1^2+x_2^2+x_3^2=a^2\). In stereographic coordinates the notes display \(\Omega=a\,dz\wedge d\bar z/(1+|z|^2)^2\), \(\omega=(a/i)(z\,d\bar z-\bar z\,dz)/(1+|z|^2)\), and a decomposition of a rotation generator into commuting holomorphic and antiholomorphic pieces.
statement: The sphere is \(\mathbb{CP}^1\). On a complex chart its real invariant area form is a real multiple of \(i\,dz\wedge d\bar z/(1+|z|^2)^2\); the coefficient is fixed by the total symplectic area. Holomorphic differential operators and their conjugates commute when their coefficients depend only on \(z\) and \(\bar z\), respectively. The two displayed forms in the notebook do not satisfy \(d\omega=\Omega\): direct differentiation gives \(d\omega=(2a/i)\,dz\wedge d\bar z/(1+|z|^2)^2\).
reconstruction: The derivative is an editorial check of the recorded formula, not a recovered replacement coefficient for the original speaker.
fate: The geometric representation mechanism is the rank-one Borel--Weil model \citep[Theorem 4]{serre1954borelweil}. The local coefficients written in the notebook require a normalization correction before they define that model.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope; no open problem is asserted by this item.

title: Integrality of the sphere representation
notes: The page says that a measure making the operators self-adjoint exists only for integral \(a\), writes a weight \((1+|z|^2)^{-a}\), and obtains a finite space of analytic polynomials.
statement: The global condition is that \([\Omega/(2\pi\hbar)]\) be an integral cohomology class. For its nonnegative degree \(k\) on \(\mathbb{CP}^1\), the holomorphic sections of \(\mathcal O(k)\) have dimension \(k+1\) and realize the irreducible \(SU(2)\) representation of highest weight \(k\); it descends to \(SO(3)\) precisely when \(k\) is even. A positive weighted measure \((1+|z|^2)^{-a}d^2z\) itself exists for every real \(a\), and is finite when \(a>1\).
reconstruction: The source parameter \(a\) is not identified with \(k\) until the missing factors of \(i,2,\hbar\) and the area-density convention are fixed. In the stated flat area measure, \(z^j\) is square-integrable exactly when \(a>j+1\); this check prevents an unsupported dimension formula.
fate: Integral line bundles and their irreducible representations are already in \citet[Theorem 4]{serre1954borelweil}; the prequantum integrality criterion is \citet[Proposition 2.1.1]{kostant1970quantization}. Thus integrality belongs to a global equivariant quantization, not to bare existence of a measure.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope; no open problem is asserted by this item.

title: Von Neumann algebras and factors
notes: A weakly closed self-adjoint operator algebra \(R\) is considered; it is a factor when its center consists of scalars.
statement: A von Neumann algebra on a complex Hilbert space \(H\) is a unital weak-operator closed \(*\)-subalgebra \(M\subset B(H)\). It is a factor if \(Z(M)=M\cap M^{\prime}=\mathbb CI\). Its abstract algebra and its particular representation on \(H\) should be distinguished.
fate: This is the classical Murray--von Neumann framework; a checked modern statement is \citet[Chapters 1 and 4]{jones2015vonneumann}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope; no open problem is asserted by this item.

title: Matrix factors and type I tensor decompositions
notes: For matrix algebras the notes write a tensor decomposition and describe minimal projections.
statement: If a factor \(M\subset B(H)\) contains a nonzero minimal projection, there are Hilbert spaces \(K,L\) and a unitary \(H\simeq K\otimes L\) such that \(M=B(K)\otimes I_L\) and \(M^{\prime}=I_K\otimes B(L)\). In finite dimensions this is the ordinary matrix-factor structure. The tensor description does not apply to arbitrary type II or III factors.
reconstruction: The minimal-projection hypothesis restricts the tensor factorization to type I.
fate: The type I characterization is classical; see \citet[Theorem 4.2.1]{jones2015vonneumann}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope; no open problem is asserted by this item.

title: Central decomposition into factors
notes: The general algebra is described as a direct integral of factors.
statement: For a von Neumann algebra acting on a separable Hilbert space, central decomposition yields a measurable field of factor algebras over a standard measure space, with the original algebra their direct integral, up to the usual almost-everywhere equivalence. The center becomes the diagonal \(L^\infty\) algebra.
fate: This is von Neumann\textquotesingle s reduction theory, published in 1949; \citet[Chapter V, Section 1]{connes1994noncommutative} gives the classical theorem and its role. It is a direct integral, not a discrete sum in general.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope; no open problem is asserted by this item.

title: Projections generate a von Neumann algebra
notes: The factor is said to be generated by its projection operators.
statement: For every self-adjoint \(x\in M\), all its spectral projections lie in \(M\), and step-function spectral approximants converge to \(x\). Since every element is a linear combination of two self-adjoint elements, the von Neumann algebra is generated by its projections.
fate: This is the spectral-theorem foundation of projection classification, recalled in \citet[Chapters 1 and 4]{jones2015vonneumann}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope; no open problem is asserted by this item.

title: Murray--von Neumann comparison and dimension
notes: Projection equivalence, comparison and addition of orthogonal projections are used to define a dimension scale.
statement: For projections \(p,q\in M\), write \(p\sim q\) when some partial isometry \(v\in M\) satisfies \(v^*v=p\), \(vv^*=q\), and write \(p\precsim q\) when \(p\) is equivalent to a subprojection of \(q\). In a factor any two projections are comparable. A normal dimension function is invariant under equivalence and additive on orthogonal sums, with normalization dependent on the type.
fate: The precise comparison statement is \citet[Definition 6.1.1 and Theorem 6.1.8]{jones2015vonneumann}; it is classical material predating the lecture.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope; no open problem is asserted by this item.

title: Factor types and projection-dimension ranges
notes: The alternatives \(I\), \(II_1\), \(II_\infty\), \(III\) are distinguished by existence of minimal projections and dimension values.
statement: For factors on a separable Hilbert space, the standard projection-dimension scales are \(\{0,1,\ldots,n\}\) for \(I_n\), \(\{0,1,2,\ldots,\infty\}\) for \(I_\infty\), \([0,1]\) for normalized \(II_1\), \([0,\infty]\) for \(II_\infty\), and \(\{0,\infty\}\) for \(III\). The type III scale records equivalence of nonzero projections in the countably decomposable factor setting; it is not a finite trace.
fate: The classical ranges and the distinction between finiteness of the identity and mere order type are explicitly set out in \citet[Section 6.1, pp.~35--37]{jones2015vonneumann}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope; no open problem is asserted by this item.

title: Trace, determinant and the limits of matrix analogy
notes: The finite factor is said to possess trace, determinant and a minimax principle, with the suggestion that matrix arguments continue.
statement: A \(II_1\) factor has a unique faithful normal tracial state \(\tau\), normalized by \(\tau(1)=1\). For invertible \(x\), the Fuglede--Kadison determinant is \(\Delta(x)=\exp\tau(\log|x|)\), a positive real number. Spectral distribution and variational analogues exist, but a general self-adjoint element need not have a discrete list of eigenvalues, and the notebook supplies no particular minimax formula.
fate: The determinant is \citet[Section 2]{fugledekadison1952determinant}; the trace is reviewed in \citet[Section 6.1]{jones2015vonneumann}. These verify the identified structures, not the unlimited phrase that all finite-matrix arguments apply.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope; no open problem is asserted by this item.

title: Uniqueness of the separable hyperfinite II1 factor
notes: The approximately finite factor is described as unique.
statement: Among \(II_1\) factors with separable predual, the hyperfinite factor is unique up to isomorphism. Here hyperfinite means generated in the weak operator topology by an increasing sequence of finite-dimensional \(*\)-subalgebras. The claim is not uniqueness of all finite factors.
fate: The uniqueness is the classical Murray--von Neumann theorem, recalled with proof sketch in \citet[Theorem 15.1.1]{jones2015vonneumann}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope; no open problem is asserted by this item.

title: Named earlier nonisomorphic factor constructions
notes: The notebook lists Schwartz, Ching, Sakai, Dixmier, Lance, Zeller-Meier, Stepin and Golodets in a compressed history of examples.
statement: The list by itself contains no specified algebra, invariant or cardinality assertion for each author. It cannot be expanded into separate priority theorems without additional source evidence.
fate: McDuff\textquotesingle s author bibliography identifies Ching, Dixmier--Lance, Sakai and Zeller-Meier as antecedents to her 1969 work \citep{mcduff1969uncountably}. That is contextual confirmation; it does not identify every construction in this notebook list.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: the historical list is preserved; no unrecorded specific theorem is assigned to every name.

title: A continuum of pairwise nonisomorphic II1 factors
notes: McDuff announces \(\mathfrak c\) nonisomorphic factors of type \(II_1\).
statement: There are \(2^{\aleph_0}\) pairwise nonisomorphic type \(II_1\) factors acting on separable Hilbert space.
fate: This is exactly the principal result of \citet{mcduff1969uncountably}, Annals 90(2), pp.~372--377. Its author abstract was read and the September 1969 issue date verified; the lecture is 6 October 1969. Hence the chronological class is E, although the speaker is the author. The full proof was not directly read in this task.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope; no open problem is asserted by this item.

title: Classifying irreducible representations of an interval current group
notes: For matrices \(u(t)\in SU(2)\), \(0\leq t\leq1\), the notes ask for irreducible unitary representations. No differentiability class or topology is written.
statement: After specifying a topological group \(G\) of \(SU(2)\)-valued maps on \([0,1]\), classify its strongly continuous irreducible unitary representations up to unitary equivalence. The choices \(C^0\), \(C^1\), \(C^\infty\), bounded measurable maps, and operator-norm versus strong continuity of the representation define different problems.
reconstruction: The topological categories are supplied for comparison, not attributed to the 1969 lecturer.
fate: \citet[Theorem 4.11; group theorem in the arXiv version, Theorem 4.15]{janssensneeb2015norm} classify the norm-continuous irreducible representations in the smooth compact-semisimple setting by finite evaluation tensors. Their preprint circulated 11 February 2013, the paper appeared online in December 2014 and in print in 2015. This is a proper subcategory of all strongly continuous representations. \citet[Chapter 1]{janssensneeb2024positive} impose positive-energy assumptions absent from the notebook; \citet[Definitions 2.1--2.3]{araki1970factorizable} use a different measurable current-group category.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: strong results exist in precisely restricted categories; the notebook\textquotesingle s unrestricted classification is not a single well-posed problem, and the checked sources do not supply a complete strong-continuity classification.
worth: Worth developing only after fixing regularity and continuity, because evaluation classification in the norm-continuous category does not control the strongly continuous category.

title: An irreducible representation with interval support
notes: The support is the smallest closed \(F\) such that \(u=1\) on a neighborhood of \(F\) implies \(T_u=I\). The explicit question is whether an irreducible representation can have a whole interval as support.
statement: For a chosen function group and continuity convention, ask for an irreducible unitary representation which is nontrivial on the subgroup of functions supported in every nonempty open subinterval. This is a precise full-support formulation of the displayed question. Norm-continuous smooth-current representations have finite support, whereas strongly continuous representations require separate analysis.
reconstruction: The direct local-subgroup criterion avoids presupposing existence of a smallest closed support for an entirely unspecified class of maps.
fate: The finite-support obstruction follows from \citet[Theorem 4.11]{janssensneeb2015norm}. The \(SU(2)\) energy irreducibility theorem of \citet{ismagilov1976unitary} assumes base dimension at least five and cannot answer an interval question; \citet[p.~74]{ismagilov1981segment} proves reducibility of the interval energy representation. The chapter develops an explicit paired-evaluation infinite tensor construction for \(C^1\) maps, also irreducible on smooth maps, and checks full interval support. It does not assert an exact archival topology or novelty.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: the bounded \(C^1\)/smooth strong-continuity existence variant is proved in this chapter; no verdict is asserted for every possible interpretation of the unspecified 1969 group.
worth: Worth developing in a fixed topology, because the contrast between finite norm-continuous support and full strongly continuous support is both explicit and mathematically consequential.

title: Single-point evaluation representations
notes: The simplest example evaluates \(u\) at \(t_0\) and applies an irreducible representation of \(SU(2)\).
statement: For \(t_0\in[0,1]\) and the irreducible \(SU(2)\) representation \(V_\ell\) of highest weight \(\ell\geq0\), \(\pi(u)=V_\ell(u(t_0))\) is irreducible because the evaluation homomorphism is onto. It is continuous for each usual \(C^r\) topology. For \(\ell>0\) its support is \(\{t_0\}\); the trivial representation has empty support.
fate: This is the elementary evaluation construction, included as the basic family in \citet{janssensneeb2015norm}. It was available before the lecture; the later theorem classifies a specified category, rather than introducing this example.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope; no open problem is asserted by this item.

title: Finite tensor products at distinct points
notes: The notes tensor evaluation representations at finitely many points and describe them as irreducible.
statement: At pairwise distinct \(t_1,\ldots,t_m\), the joint evaluation from \(C^r([0,1],SU(2))\) onto \(SU(2)^m\) is surjective for \(r=0,1,\ldots,\infty\). Thus the tensor product of irreducible factor representations is irreducible, with support the finite subset carrying nontrivial factors. Repeated evaluation points must first be combined and decomposed as \(SU(2)\) tensor products.
reconstruction: Distinctness, removal of trivial factors and the regularity convention are made explicit.
fate: The finite evaluation family is precisely the one in \citet{janssensneeb2015norm}. The interpolation and irreducibility argument is classical and does not depend on the later completeness theorem.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope; no open problem is asserted by this item.

title: The countably many evaluation points remark
notes: The source says that the construction cannot be done for a countable set, followed by a parenthesis that it can be done for a convergent sequence.
statement: An infinite tensor product requires choices of reference vectors and convergence conditions for the product unitaries; continuity and irreducibility are additional issues. Cardinality alone is not an obstruction, and the recorded parenthesis provides too little information to recover the intended construction or exclusion theorem.
fate: \citet[Section 4]{araki1970factorizable} analyzes discrete and continuous tensor contributions in a specified measurable setting. The chapter\textquotesingle s paired-evaluation construction also demonstrates why a bare prohibition for countable sets is untenable without a category and tensor-sector convention.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: the exact intended claim is unidentified; one cannot infer a general nonexistence theorem from this sentence.

title: Exponential Hilbert space and coherent vectors
notes: The notes define \(e^K\) as the sum of symmetric tensor powers and write exponential vectors with normalization \(\sqrt{p!}\).
statement: For a complex Hilbert space \(K\), let \(\Gamma_s(K)=\bigoplus_{p=0}^{\infty}\operatorname{Sym}^pK\), where the zeroth summand is \(\mathbb C\). Define \(e(\phi)=\bigoplus_{p\geq0}\phi^{\otimes p}/\sqrt{p!}\). Then \(\langle e(\phi),e(\psi)\rangle=\exp\langle\phi,\psi\rangle\), and these vectors span a dense subspace.
reconstruction: The tensor factor repeated in degree p is phi; the handwritten final factor and the distinction between the degree index and vector must not alter the coherent-vector definition.
fate: This is classical symmetric Fock space, used explicitly in \citet[Section 4]{araki1970factorizable}; his paper was submitted in June 1969 and revised in November, and builds on earlier exponential-space work cited there.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope; no open problem is asserted by this item.

title: Fock factorization over orthogonal sums
notes: The identity \(e^{K_1\oplus K_2}=e^{K_1}\otimes e^{K_2}\) is used to motivate a continuous product.
statement: There is a canonical unitary \(\Gamma_s(K_1\oplus K_2)\simeq\Gamma_s(K_1)\otimes\Gamma_s(K_2)\) carrying \(e(\phi_1\oplus\phi_2)\) to \(e(\phi_1)\otimes e(\phi_2)\). It follows by comparing exponential inner products and using their dense spans; direct-integral versions require a specified measurable field and measure.
fate: The exponential-space factorization is the framework of \citet[Sections 3--4]{araki1970factorizable}. The displayed finite-sum identity is established independently of any irreducibility claim for a current group.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope; no open problem is asserted by this item.

title: A reducible direct-integral Fock representation
notes: The notes pass to \(K=\int^\oplus K(t)\,dt\) and explicitly observe that the representation constructed in Fock space is reducible.
statement: If \(\rho(u)\) is the decomposable unitary action on a nonzero direct-integral one-particle space, its second quantization \(\Gamma_s(\rho(u))=\bigoplus_{p\geq0}\operatorname{Sym}^p\rho(u)\) preserves each particle-number summand. In particular the vacuum line is invariant, so this representation is reducible whenever a nonzero positive-degree summand is present.
reconstruction: The exact action is not written fully, so the number-preserving interpretation is stated as the version verified by the recorded direct-integral example.
fate: Araki\textquotesingle s more general formulas include cocycle displacement terms \citep[Section 4, Lemma 4.2]{araki1970factorizable}; they must not be identified with the simpler number-preserving construction. The notebook\textquotesingle s stated reducibility is correct for the latter.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope; no open problem is asserted by this item.

title: Abelian characters from linear functionals
notes: For \(\alpha(t)=\exp x(t)\), a character is written as an exponential of a linear functional or generalized function; delta mass gives point evaluation.
statement: On the additive real space \(C^\infty([0,1],\mathbb R)\), every continuous real linear functional \(T\) gives the unitary character \(f\mapsto\exp(iT(f))\). It descends along \(f\mapsto e^{if}\) to the smooth \(U(1)\) current group on the interval exactly when \(T(1)\in\mathbb Z\), because two lifts differ by a constant multiple of \(2\pi\). Point evaluation corresponds to a delta functional. For the uniform \(C^0\) topology, continuous functionals are finite signed measures, rather than arbitrary distributions.
reconstruction: The factor i, real-valuedness and integral-period condition are supplied to make the formula a unitary group character; the notebook uses informal complex exponential notation.
fate: The abelian factorizable setting is discussed in \citet[Sections 1--2 and 9]{araki1970factorizable}. The interval lifting condition and the topology-dependent dual clarify the notebook\textquotesingle s schematic exponential formula; no classification of nonabelian irreducibles follows from it.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope; no open problem is asserted by this item.

title: Unspecified singular-value inequalities
notes: The heading \ru{О s-числах} is followed by Gantmacher, Wielandt, Berezin--Gelfand, Weyl and Ky Fan, with a reference to Trudy MMO and semisimple groups.
statement: Singular values of a compact operator are the eigenvalues of its absolute value, counted with multiplicity. The notebook does not state which inequality, representation-theoretic construction or extension to semisimple groups is intended.
fate: The checked Fourier-inequality literature confirms the use of Schatten norms, but does not identify an individual theorem from this list. No result is assigned solely on the basis of the named authors.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: the precise singular-value claim remains unidentified; the names and publication hint are retained as a research lead.

title: Weighted Schatten norms for the compact-group Fourier transform
notes: The displayed \(p\)-norm is a sum over irreducibles weighted by \(d_\sigma\), but lacks a readable final exponent and a closing argument parenthesis.
statement: For a compact group \(G\) with normalized Haar measure, let \(\widehat G\) denote the unitary irreducibles and \(\widehat f(\sigma)=\int_G f(g)\sigma(g)^*\,dg\). For \(1\leq p<\infty\), put \(\|A\|_{\ell^p(\widehat G)}=(\sum_\sigma d_\sigma\operatorname{Tr}|A_\sigma|^p)^{1/p}\); for \(p=\infty\), use \(\sup_\sigma\|A_\sigma\|_{\mathrm{op}}\). The sum is interpreted over the finite-support partial sums if the dual is uncountable.
reconstruction: Normalized Haar measure, Schatten rather than entrywise norms, and the exponent \(1/p\) are made explicit.
fate: These are the standard compact-group Fourier norms used in the compact-group case described by \citet[pp.~293--294]{russo1974fourier} and in \citet{hewittross1970abstract}. The missing root is a mathematical emendation, not an established reading of the handwriting.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope; no open problem is asserted by this item.

title: Peter--Weyl--Plancherel identity
notes: The notebook states \(\|\widehat f\|_2^2=\int_G|f|^2\,d\lambda\).
statement: For a compact group with Haar probability measure and \(f\in L^2(G)\), \(\sum_{\sigma\in\widehat G}d_\sigma\operatorname{Tr}(\widehat f(\sigma)^*\widehat f(\sigma))=\|f\|_2^2\). Equivalently, the Fourier transform extends to a unitary onto the Hilbert direct sum of the matrix spaces with these weights.
fate: This is the classical compact-group Plancherel theorem. The exact probability-Haar formula was checked in \citet[Theorem 5.1, p.~6]{sakellaridisndcompact}; the older book treatment is \citet[Theorem 28.43]{hewittross1970abstract}. Neither later exposition is asserted to be the origin of the theorem.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope; no open problem is asserted by this item.

title: Compact-group Riemann--Lebesgue lemma
notes: For every \(f\in L^1(G)\) and \(\varepsilon>0\), only finitely many irreducibles have Fourier coefficient operator norm larger than \(\varepsilon\).
statement: For a compact group and \(f\in L^1(G)\), the field \(\widehat f(\sigma)\) vanishes at infinity in operator norm on the discrete dual: \(\{\sigma:\|\widehat f(\sigma)\|_{\mathrm{op}}>\varepsilon\}\) is finite for every \(\varepsilon>0\). Approximation by finite linear combinations of matrix coefficients proves the assertion, using \(\|\widehat f(\sigma)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\leq\|f\|_1\).
reconstruction: The short approximation proof is supplied to make the precise operator-norm conclusion explicit.
fate: The finite-matrix-coefficient density statement was checked in \citet[Proposition 4.5, p.~5]{sakellaridisndcompact}. Together with the displayed \(L^1\)-to-operator-norm estimate it gives the recorded conclusion: first approximate by a finite Fourier polynomial, then bound every remaining coefficient by the approximation error. This is classical Peter--Weyl theory.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope; no open problem is asserted by this item.

title: Kunze--Hausdorff--Young inequality
notes: The notes attribute \(\|\widehat f\|_{p^{\prime}}\leq\|f\|_p\), \(1<p<2\), to Kunze and label it Hausdorff--Young.
statement: Let \(G\) be compact with Haar probability measure and \(1\leq p\leq2\), \(p^{\prime}=p/(p-1)\). Then \(\|\widehat f\|_{\ell^{p^{\prime}}(\widehat G)}\leq\|f\|_{L^p(G)}\), with the \(p=1\) target interpreted in operator norm. The coefficient norm is the weighted Schatten norm, not a scalar norm on matrix entries.
fate: Kunze published the unimodular-group extension in 1958, as explicitly documented in \citet[Introduction and reference 8]{russo1974fourier}. Its compact specialization is the theorem in the notes; this also continues the earlier seminar discussion 1967-137.11.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope; no open problem is asserted by this item.

title: Equality on the circle
notes: The Hardy--Littlewood theorem is stated as equality only for \(f(x)=\alpha e^{inx}\).
statement: For \(1<p<2\) and nonzero \(f\in L^p(\mathbb T)\), equality in Hausdorff--Young holds exactly when \(f(x)=c e^{inx}\) almost everywhere, for some nonzero \(c\in\mathbb C\) and \(n\in\mathbb Z\). The zero function is an additional trivial equality case; at the endpoint \(p=2\), all functions give equality.
fate: The circle statement is the classical Hardy--Littlewood equality case, discussed as the antecedent of the compact-group result in \citet[pp.~293--294]{russo1974fourier}. It follows as well from the compact-group characterization, because the circle has no proper open subgroup.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope; no open problem is asserted by this item.

title: Compact-group Hausdorff--Young extremizers
notes: The general-group examples are continuous multiplicative functions on an open subgroup \(G_0\), equal to one at the identity and extended by zero outside \(G_0\).
statement: For a compact group \(G\), \(1<p<2\), and nonzero \(f\in L^p(G)\), equality holds exactly for functions \(f(x)=c\chi(x_0^{-1}x)\mathbf1_{x_0H}(x)\) almost everywhere, where \(H\) is an open subgroup, \(\chi:H\to U(1)\) is a continuous character, \(x_0\in G\), and \(c\ne0\). Openness makes \(H\) compact; translation and scalar multiplication preserve the equality.
reconstruction: The complete classification, including almost-everywhere equality, translates and scalar multiples, is supplied from the published result.
fate: The compact-group result appears in \citet[Section 43]{hewittross1970abstract}, published in 1970 after this November 1969 lecture. \citet[Theorem 1 and pp.~293--294]{russo1974fourier} states the broader unimodular theorem and expressly credits Hewitt--Ross for the compact case. The exact theorem was read in Russo; the original book was checked through publisher metadata and this explicit attribution. The notebook provides subgroup representatives and omits translates and scalar multiples from the final line.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: the compact-group equality classification is established. The verified chronology is the 17 November 1969 seminar report followed by the 1970 book; no earlier circulation date or absolute priority is inferred from the checked evidence.

title: Interpolation behind Fourier norm inequalities
notes: The closing sentence says that analogues of the Riesz--Thorin theorems exist.
statement: The Fourier map has endpoint bounds \(L^1(G)\to\ell^\infty(\widehat G)\) and \(L^2(G)\to\ell^2(\widehat G)\). Interpolation in the weighted Schatten spaces gives the compact Hausdorff--Young estimate at intermediate exponents. The sentence does not identify any additional interpolation theorem or a different operator.
reconstruction: The endpoint spaces and resulting interpolation application are supplied as an interpretation of the brief remark.
fate: This is the standard interpolation mechanism in the Hausdorff--Young theory discussed by \citet[Introduction]{russo1974fourier} and \citet[Section 43]{hewittross1970abstract}. Only this explicit application is reconstructed; no unspecified stronger analogue is claimed.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope; no open problem is asserted by this item.

title: Quasi-unipotence and the monodromy exponent
notes: For monodromy \(T:H^i(V_s)\to H^i(V_s)\), the notes state \((T^N-1)^{i+1}=0\) for some \(N\), then call \(T\) unipotent.
statement: For a smooth projective family of complex algebraic varieties over a punctured smooth algebraic curve, local monodromy on \(H^i\) has roots of unity as eigenvalues, and for some positive integer \(N\), \((T^N-I)^{i+1}=0\). Thus \(T\) is quasi-unipotent; after the base change \(z=w^N\), monodromy is unipotent with nilpotency index at most \(i+1\).
reconstruction: Smoothness and projectivity over the punctured curve are sufficient modern hypotheses. The correction concerns the separate parenthesis, not the correctly written power of monodromy.
fate: \citet[Theorem 3.1, pp.~235--236]{griffiths1970periods} states this theorem and discusses the proofs of Landman, Clemens and Grothendieck. The survey was submitted 18 September 1969 and published March 1970, after an invited lecture on 29 August 1968; the result predates the February 1970 seminar report.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope; no open problem is asserted by this item.

title: The cohomology local system and Gauss--Manin bundle
notes: The bundle \(W\to S\) has algebraic-curve base; \(\pi_1(S)\) acts on fibre cohomology. The associated analytic vector bundle is trivial with parallel transport on the universal cover.
statement: For a smooth proper morphism \(\pi:W\to S\) of complex algebraic varieties, \(\mathcal L=R^i\pi_*\mathbb C\) is a finite-rank local system. Its analytic bundle \(E=\mathcal L\otimes_{\mathbb C}\mathcal O_S\) has the canonical flat Gauss--Manin connection, with horizontal sections \(\mathcal L\). Pullback to a simply connected covering trivializes the local system and its flat bundle.
fate: This is the classical construction recalled in \citet[Section 2, pp.~231--233]{griffiths1970periods}. The notebook\textquotesingle s phrase algebraic bundle is replaced by an explicit smooth proper family, not an arbitrary algebraic map.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope; no open problem is asserted by this item.

title: Picard--Fuchs equations in a local frame
notes: The first abbreviated line reads \(\partial/\partial z=A(z)\); the next complete line says every flat section satisfies \(f^{\prime}(z)=A(z)f(z)\), and conversely.
statement: In a local frame of a flat holomorphic vector bundle on a complex curve, a horizontal section with coefficient column \(u(z)\) satisfies a first-order system \(u^{\prime}(z)=A(z)u(z)\), with the sign determined by the connection-matrix convention. Conversely every solution determines a horizontal section. Changes of frame transform the coefficient matrix by the usual gauge formula.
reconstruction: The vector of coefficients and the connection sign convention are specified; the abbreviated first line is not treated as an equality of an operator with a matrix.
fate: The local connection equation is standard and is used explicitly in \citet[Section 4]{griffiths1970periods}. The complete equation in the notebook resolves the earlier operator abbreviation.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope; no open problem is asserted by this item.

title: Periods pair moving cycles with cohomology
notes: The notes transport a cycle \(\phi_z\subset V_z\) and write \((f_i(z),\phi_z)\), described as the value of cohomology on homology and a vector function.
statement: A locally constant family of homology classes \(\gamma_z\in H_i(V_z,\mathbb C)\) is horizontal for the dual Gauss--Manin connection. For a local cohomology frame \(\omega_j(z)\), the period functions \(\langle\omega_j(z),\gamma_z\rangle\) satisfy the induced dual differential system. They are not individually constant unless the corresponding cohomology classes also are horizontal.
reconstruction: The flat cycle lies in the homology local system; period coordinates are obtained by pairing with the chosen cohomology frame.
fate: The homology--cohomology pairing and period system are the construction in \citet[Sections 2 and 4]{griffiths1970periods}. This identifies the recorded cycle example while keeping the bundle and its dual distinct.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope; no open problem is asserted by this item.

title: Regular singularity of the Gauss--Manin connection
notes: The theorem attributed to Griffiths says that a basis can be chosen with \(zA(z)\) holomorphic at the puncture.
statement: For the Gauss--Manin connection of a smooth projective algebraic family over a punctured curve, there is a logarithmic extension across each puncture: in a local holomorphic frame of that extension, the connection matrix has at most a simple pole. Equivalently, starting with an algebraic meromorphic frame, the system is regular singular. An arbitrary holomorphic gauge on the punctured disk can introduce worse apparent growth.
reconstruction: The basis is a frame of an extension, or an admissible meromorphic frame; the assertion is not invariant under unrestricted holomorphic gauges on a punctured disk.
fate: \citet[Theorem 4.3, p.~238]{griffiths1970periods} states regularity and explains its relation to the monodromy theorem. The article was submitted in September 1969; publication in March 1970 does not make this a post-seminar discovery.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope; no open problem is asserted by this item.

title: Puiseux--logarithmic local expansions
notes: The displayed flat-section series has fractional powers \(z^{n/N}\) and finitely many powers of \(\log z\); its lower-index handwriting is uncertain and is transcribed as \(n\leq0\).
statement: After choosing a branch on a sector and a meromorphic frame, regular singularity with quasi-unipotent monodromy gives a convergent expansion \(\sum_{n\geq n_0}z^{n/N}\sum_{j=0}^{i}c_{nj}(\log z)^j\) for horizontal degree-\(i\) sections, for some integer \(n_0\) and positive integer \(N\). The coefficients are vectors. There are only finitely many negative powers after ramification, and logarithmic degree is bounded by the monodromy nilpotency index minus one.
reconstruction: The finite principal part, sector, coefficient vectors and direction of summation are explicit additions needed for a correct local expansion.
fate: The factorization of a fundamental solution into a meromorphic factor and a monodromy exponential is described by \citet[pp.~238--239]{griffiths1970periods}; it gives exactly this expansion under the stated hypotheses. The index is mathematically reconstructed rather than claimed as a certain decipherment.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope; no open problem is asserted by this item.

title: Moderate growth of periods near a puncture
notes: The lemma bounds any flat section by \(C|z|^{-a}|\log z|^b\).
statement: In a meromorphic frame of the regular-singular Gauss--Manin bundle, on each sufficiently small sector with a fixed bounded range of argument, every horizontal section satisfies \(\|u(z)\|\leq C|z|^{-a}(1+|\log z|)^b\), for suitable constants depending on the section and sector. A freely chosen holomorphic frame with an essential singularity would invalidate this statement.
fate: The moderate-growth characterization is explained in \citet[pp.~238--239]{griffiths1970periods}, and follows directly from the preceding Puiseux--log expansion. This is a theorem in the specified geometric and gauge category, not a universal estimate for flat analytic connections.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope; no open problem is asserted by this item.

title: Affine spectra as ringed spaces
notes: A scheme is introduced as a topological space with a structure sheaf of rings; for an affine scheme, its points are prime ideals of a commutative ring with identity.
statement: For a commutative unital ring \(A\), \(\operatorname{Spec}A\) consists of its proper prime ideals. Equipped with the Zariski topology and structure sheaf, it is an affine scheme; its stalk at \(\mathfrak p\) is the local ring \(A_{\mathfrak p}\). The zero ring has empty spectrum. A scheme is a locally ringed space covered by such affine models.
fate: This is the established Grothendieck framework of \citet{grothendieck1960ega1}; its current formulation is checked in \citet[Section 26.5]{stacks2026foundations}. It continues the seminar foundations of 1965-85.1 and 1968-163.1--2.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope; no open problem is asserted by this item.

title: Zariski topology and principal-open basis
notes: For an ideal \(I\), \(U_I\) comprises primes not containing \(I\). The exercises ask that these sets form a topology and that the sets \(U_f\) form a basis.
statement: With \(D(I)=\{\mathfrak p:I\not\subseteq\mathfrak p\}\), one has \(D(I)=\bigcup_{f\in I}D(f)\), \(D(f)\cap D(g)=D(fg)\), \(D(0)=\varnothing\), and \(D(1)=\operatorname{Spec}A\). These identities prove that the \(D(I)\) are precisely the opens of a topology and that the principal opens form a basis.
fate: These are the standard elementary spectrum identities, checked in \citet[Lemma 10.17.2]{stacks2026foundations}, within the foundational theory already published in \citet{grothendieck1960ega1}. The displayed identities resolve both exercises.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope; no open problem is asserted by this item.

title: The spectrum is a T0 space
notes: The exercise asks for the weakest separation axiom: of two points, one can be separated from the other by a neighborhood.
statement: For distinct prime ideals \(\mathfrak p,\mathfrak q\), choose an element in their symmetric difference. Its principal open contains exactly one of the two points. Thus \(\operatorname{Spec}A\) is \(T_0\); it is generally neither \(T_1\) nor Hausdorff.
fate: This is an immediate consequence of the spectrum topology in \citet[Section 10.17]{stacks2026foundations}. It is a classical exercise, and no stronger separation property is inferred.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope; no open problem is asserted by this item.

title: Localization and the equality of fractions
notes: The localization uses a multiplicative set \(S\) excluding zero and identifies \(a/s\) and \(a^{\prime}/s^{\prime}\) when some \(s^{\prime\prime}\in S\) kills \(s^{\prime}a-sa^{\prime}\). The exercise asks for equivalence of this relation.
statement: For a multiplicative set \(S\subset A\) containing \(1\), the relation \((a,s)\sim(a^{\prime},s^{\prime})\) iff \(t(s^{\prime}a-sa^{\prime})=0\) for some \(t\in S\) is reflexive, symmetric and transitive; fraction addition and multiplication make the quotient \(S^{-1}A\). If \(0\in S\), this is the zero ring. For modules the same formula replaces \(a\) by a module element.
reconstruction: The conventional condition that 1 belongs to S, and the harmless zero-ring case needed by the next construction, are supplied.
fate: This is the standard localization construction used throughout \citet{grothendieck1960ega1} and \citet[Section 10.9]{stacks2026foundations}. Allowing the zero ring is necessary to include \(A_f\) when \(f\) is nilpotent and its principal open is empty.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope; no open problem is asserted by this item.

title: The structure sheaf from localizations
notes: The structure sheaf is specified by \(\Gamma(U_f,\mathcal O)=A_{\{f^n\}}\).
statement: There is a sheaf of rings \(\mathcal O_X\) on \(X=\operatorname{Spec}A\) with \(\Gamma(D(f),\mathcal O_X)=A_f\), compatible with localization restriction maps. Its stalk at \(\mathfrak p\) is \(A_{\mathfrak p}\), so it is a sheaf of local rings at points, and \(\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)=A\).
fate: The result is foundational scheme theory; the explicit construction and section and stalk identifications are checked in \citet[Lemma 26.5.4]{stacks2026foundations}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope; no open problem is asserted by this item.

title: The sheaf equalizer and its two restriction arrows
notes: The diagram uses circled-plus signs, but its caption says product of sets. The question asks why there are two arrows to the sections on intersections.
statement: A presheaf \(F\) of sets is a sheaf if, for every open cover \(U=\bigcup U_\alpha\), the map \(F(U)\to\prod_\alpha F(U_\alpha)\) identifies \(F(U)\) with the equalizer of two maps to \(\prod_{\alpha,\beta}F(U_\alpha\cap U_\beta)\). Their \((\alpha,\beta)\)-components restrict \(s_\alpha\) and \(s_\beta\), respectively; the target open is the same, but the input component differs.
reconstruction: The product meaning follows the prose caption; the overwritten source index in the second arrow is not treated as a secure alpha.
fate: This is the standard gluing and uniqueness axiom, checked in \citet[Section 6.7]{stacks2026foundations}. Products, not direct sums, permit arbitrary compatible local families. The written caption supports reading the symbol as an informal product notation.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope; no open problem is asserted by this item.

title: Stalks and canonical sheafification
notes: After mentioning stalks, the exercise asks for a unique sheaf with the same stalks as any presheaf.
statement: For a presheaf \(F\) of sets or abelian groups, there is a sheaf \(aF\) and a canonical morphism \(F\to aF\) inducing an isomorphism on every stalk. It is characterized by \(\operatorname{Hom}(aF,G)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}(F,G)\) for each sheaf \(G\), and is unique up to unique isomorphism compatible with this morphism. Merely prescribing abstract stalks without the specialization and local-section data does not determine a sheaf.
reconstruction: Uniqueness is relative to the canonical map or universal property, not an assertion about a bare collection of stalks.
fate: Canonical sheafification is classical; \citet[Lemmas 6.17.1--6.17.3]{stacks2026foundations} gives the construction and universal property. The seminar had already recorded it in 1968-152.4; it recurs below in 1970-187.7.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope; no open problem is asserted by this item.

title: Constructing a sheaf from a basis
notes: The remark says that to define a sheaf it is enough to know a presheaf on a basis.
statement: A sheaf is uniquely determined by its values and restrictions on a topological basis. Conversely, basis data extend to a sheaf with those basis values when they satisfy the sheaf gluing and uniqueness conditions for covers of basis opens by basis opens. An arbitrary presheaf on a basis can be sheafified, but its original values need not be preserved.
fate: The precise construction is \citet[Section 6.30]{stacks2026foundations}; it is the established method used in the structure-sheaf construction. The extra basis sheaf condition is essential to the literal converse.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope; no open problem is asserted by this item.

title: Principal-open inclusions, radicals and restriction maps
notes: The notes write \(U_f\subset U_g\) iff a power of \(f\) is divisible by \(g\), refer to the intersection of prime ideals, and then give the induced fraction map.
statement: For \(f,g\in A\), \(D(f)\subseteq D(g)\) iff \(f\in\sqrt{(g)}\), equivalently \(f^m=gh\) for some \(m\geq1\), \(h\in A\). Then the restriction \(A_g\to A_f\) sends \(a/g^k\) to \(ah^k/f^{mk}\). The algebraic fact is \(\sqrt I=\bigcap_{\mathfrak p\supseteq I}\mathfrak p\); the intersection of all primes is the nilradical \(\sqrt{(0)}\).
reconstruction: The radical is explicitly the radical of an ideal; the unqualified intersection of all prime ideals means the nilradical.
fate: These are standard localization and radical identities, checked in \citet[Lemmas 10.17.2 and 26.5.1]{stacks2026foundations}. The mismatched quantifier and exponent in the source are normalized to a single integer.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope; no open problem is asserted by this item.

title: Local affine models and the older word prescheme
notes: A prescheme is defined as a ringed space locally isomorphic to an affine scheme.
statement: In current terminology a scheme is a locally ringed space admitting an open cover by affine schemes. The older word prescheme used here imposes no separatedness; the notebook reserves scheme for the later diagonal-closed condition.
fate: This is historical terminology from the early EGA framework \citep{grothendieck1960ega1}. The modern definition is checked in \citet[Section 26.5]{stacks2026foundations}. The change is terminological, not a defect in the underlying construction.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope; no open problem is asserted by this item.

title: Principal opens are affine schemes
notes: The exercise asks that \((U_f,\mathcal O)\) be affine for every \(f\in A\).
statement: The canonical map \(\operatorname{Spec}A_f\to\operatorname{Spec}A\) is an isomorphism of locally ringed spaces onto \(D(f)\) equipped with the restricted structure sheaf. In particular this also covers the empty scheme when \(A_f=0\).
fate: This is part of the basic affine-spectrum theorem, checked in \citet[Lemmas 10.17.6 and 26.5.4]{stacks2026foundations}. It supplies the local compatibility required in the definition of a scheme.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope; no open problem is asserted by this item.

title: Affine fibre products and tensor products of rings
notes: The product is written \(\operatorname{Spec}A\times\operatorname{Spec}B=\operatorname{Spec}(A\otimes B)\), followed by an exercise on general preschemes.
statement: For commutative \(R\)-algebras \(A,B\), the fibre product over \(\operatorname{Spec}R\) is \(\operatorname{Spec}A\times_{\operatorname{Spec}R}\operatorname{Spec}B\simeq\operatorname{Spec}(A\otimes_RB)\). It satisfies the categorical fibre-product universal property. An unqualified product of schemes is over \(\operatorname{Spec}\mathbb Z\).
fate: The affine formula and universal property are checked in \citet[Lemma 26.17.2]{stacks2026foundations}; they are foundational scheme theory already available in \citet{grothendieck1960ega1}. The base ring cannot be omitted when working over a fixed field or base scheme.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope; no open problem is asserted by this item.

title: The empty product of the two residue-field spectra
notes: The boxed example says \(\operatorname{Spec}\mathbb Z_2\times\operatorname{Spec}\mathbb Z_3\) is empty.
statement: Interpreting \(\mathbb Z_2=\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z\) and \(\mathbb Z_3=\mathbb Z/3\mathbb Z\), the product over \(\operatorname{Spec}\mathbb Z\) is empty: the tensor product of the rings is zero, because both 2 and 3 annihilate it and \(3-2=1\). This is not the Cartesian product of the underlying one-point sets.
reconstruction: The interpretation of the two subscripted rings and the base are made explicit.
fate: The statement follows directly from the affine fibre-product formula \citep[Lemma 26.17.2]{stacks2026foundations}. The source notation is read as residue fields, not as rings of 2-adic and 3-adic integers.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope; no open problem is asserted by this item.

title: Kirillov: gluing products from affine charts
notes: The framed Kirillov intervention covers \(X,Y\) by affine opens, forms their products, and refines their overlaps; its lemma says products of open inclusions are open inclusions.
statement: Given schemes \(X,Y\) over \(S\), choose affine covers over affine opens of \(S\). The affine products \(U_\alpha\times_S V_\beta\) glue along their canonical overlap products. Base change preserves open immersions, so these pieces form an open cover of \(X\times_SY\), and the affine universal properties glue uniquely to the global one. Both cover indices range independently.
fate: The precise gluing statement and open-immersion property are \citet[Lemmas 26.17.3--26.17.4 and 26.17.6]{stacks2026foundations}. This explains the improvisation without interpreting the illegible union subscript as a new mathematical restriction.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope; no open problem is asserted by this item.
speaker: A. A. Kirillov

title: Separatedness and the affine diagonal exercise
notes: A prescheme is called a scheme if its diagonal in the product is closed; the exercise asks that an affine scheme satisfy this condition.
statement: A morphism \(X\to S\) is separated when \(\Delta_{X/S}:X\to X\times_SX\) is a closed immersion. Every affine morphism is separated: for \(X=\operatorname{Spec}A\) over \(\operatorname{Spec}R\), the diagonal is induced by the surjective multiplication map \(A\otimes_RA\to A\). For a scheme over \(S\), its diagonal is an immersion, so closed image is an equivalent criterion.
fate: The modern definition and affine proof are \citet[Lemmas 26.21.1--26.21.2 and Definition 26.21.3]{stacks2026foundations}. The lecture uses an older naming convention in which separated schemes alone are called schemes.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope; no open problem is asserted by this item.

title: Quasi-coherent modules by local free presentations
notes: A sheaf of \(\mathcal O_X\)-modules is quasi-coherent if locally it is a cokernel \(\mathcal O^{(S)}\to\mathcal O^{(T)}\), with arbitrary sets of summands.
statement: On a scheme \(X\), an \(\mathcal O_X\)-module \(\mathcal F\) is quasi-coherent iff locally it admits an exact presentation \(\mathcal O_U^{(S)}\to\mathcal O_U^{(T)}\to\mathcal F|_U\to0\), where the free sheaves are direct sums indexed by arbitrary sets. On an affine open \(U=\operatorname{Spec}A\), this is equivalent to \(\mathcal F|_U\simeq\widetilde M\) for an \(A\)-module.
fate: The equivalence is checked in \citet[Lemma 26.7.4 and Section 17.10]{stacks2026foundations}. No finiteness of the index sets is part of quasi-coherence itself.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope; no open problem is asserted by this item.

title: An example of a non-quasi-coherent module sheaf
notes: The exercise asks for a sheaf that is not quasi-coherent.
statement: Let \(X=\operatorname{Spec}k[t]\), \(U=D(t)\), and \(j:U\hookrightarrow X\). Extension by zero \(j_!\mathcal O_U\), considered as an \(\mathcal O_X\)-module, is nonzero but has no nonzero global section: a nonzero regular function on the irreducible open \(U\) has support all of \(U\), whose closure contains the missing origin. The affine equivalence would force any quasi-coherent sheaf with zero global module to vanish. Thus \(j_!\mathcal O_U\) is a counterexample.
reconstruction: The notebook contains only the question; the explicit affine-line example and verification are supplied by the companion.
fate: The exercise is classical; the supplied example is a direct application of extension by zero \citep[Lemma 6.31.6]{stacks2026foundations} and the affine equivalence \citep[Lemma 26.7.5]{stacks2026foundations}. It is an explanatory solution constructed here, not a new research result.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope; no open problem is asserted by this item.

title: The affine module--sheaf equivalence
notes: The notes call \(\mathcal F\mapsto\Gamma(\operatorname{Spec}A,\mathcal F)\) an isomorphism from quasi-coherent sheaves to modules, and say global sections determine the sheaf.
statement: For a commutative ring \(A\), the functors \(M\mapsto\widetilde M\) and \(\mathcal F\mapsto\Gamma(\operatorname{Spec}A,\mathcal F)\) are mutually quasi-inverse equivalences between \(A\)-modules and quasi-coherent \(\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}A}\)-modules. The identifications \(M\simeq\Gamma(\widetilde M)\) and \(\widetilde{\Gamma(\mathcal F)}\simeq\mathcal F\) are natural; literal equality of the categories is unnecessary.
reconstruction: The word isomorphism is interpreted as categorical equivalence with the canonical natural isomorphisms.
fate: This is standard affine scheme theory, checked in \citet[Lemma 26.7.5]{stacks2026foundations}, with antecedents in \citet{serre1955coherent} and its general-ring formulation in \citet{grothendieck1960ega1}. It is developed again in record 190.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope; no open problem is asserted by this item.

title: Vanishing of positive-degree quasi-coherent cohomology on affines
notes: The separate parenthesis says that for affine spaces the cohomology is zero, without degrees or coefficients.
statement: If \(X=\operatorname{Spec}A\) and \(\mathcal F\) is quasi-coherent, then \(H^q(X,\mathcal F)=0\) for every \(q>0\). Degree zero is the generally nonzero module of global sections. The assertion concerns affine schemes and quasi-coherent coefficients, not arbitrary sheaves on an affine topological space.
reconstruction: Positive degree and quasi-coherent coefficients are indispensable qualifications.
fate: The classical affine acyclicity theorem is checked in \citet[Lemma 30.2.2]{stacks2026foundations}, following \citet{serre1955coherent} and \citet{grothendieck1957homological}. Exactness of global sections on quasi-coherent modules is related to the affine equivalence, but the notebook\textquotesingle s unqualified equivalence phrase is not itself a proof of sheaf-cohomological vanishing.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated scope; no open problem is asserted by this item.

title: Direct image of a sheaf
